statement.text:
Suppose that a finite group G has a σi -Hall subgroup for every i ∈ I. Suppose
that a subgroup A ⩽ G is such that A ∩ H is a σi -Hall subgroup of A for every i ∈ I
and every σi -Hall subgroup H of G (see 19.84 in Archive). Is it true that then A is
σ-subnormal in G?
   An affirmative answer is known if σ = {{2}, {3}, . . .} and if G is σ-soluble.
                                                                              A. N. Skiba
